title: PFWIM Workflow
text: vignette demonstrates use PFWIM package infer consumer–resource interactions trait data, generate hypothetical realized food webs using power-law link distribution. workflow demonstrates: Inferring feasible interactions infer_edgelist(). Downsampling interactions hypothetical realized webs powerlaw_prey(). Customizing link distributions via func argument. Users can now use realised webs network analyses, simulation studies, comparisons fossil modern food webs.
code: library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(pfwim)  # Load example data included in the package data("traits", package = "pfwim") data("feeding_rules", package = "pfwim")

title: PFWIM Workflow
text: Infer interactions using categorical trait rules
code: edgelist <- infer_edgelist(   data = traits,   cat_combo_list = feeding_rules,   col_taxon = "species",   certainty_req = "all",   hide_printout = TRUE )  head(edgelist) ## # A tibble: 6 × 2 ##   taxon_resource taxon_consumer ##   <chr>          <chr>          ## 1 cod            orca           ## 2 cod            polar_bear     ## 3 deer           lynx           ## 4 deer           polar_bear     ## 5 lynx           lynx           ## 6 lynx           polar_bear

title: PFWIM Workflow
text: Generate 5 hypothetical realised webs
code: realised_webs <- powerlaw_prey(   el = edgelist,   n_samp = 5,   y = 2.5 )  # Inspect first realised web realised_webs[[1]] ##      resource   consumer ## 9    plankton        cod ## 14    plant_2       deer ## 11    plant_1       deer ## 20       seal       lynx ## 3        deer       lynx ## 16 polar_bear       orca ## 7        orca       orca ## 2         cod polar_bear ## 22       seal polar_bear ## 4        deer polar_bear ## 19        rat polar_bear ## 12    plant_1        rat ## 10   plankton       seal

title: PFWIM Workflow
code: # Define a custom in-degree distribution function custom_func <- function(r, M, y) (M - r + 1)^(-y)  realised_webs_custom <- powerlaw_prey(   el = edgelist,   n_samp = 5,   y = 2,   func = custom_func )  # First custom web realised_webs_custom[[1]] ##      resource   consumer ## 9    plankton        cod ## 14    plant_2       deer ## 18        rat       lynx ## 5        lynx       lynx ## 1         cod       orca ## 7        orca       orca ## 16 polar_bear       orca ## 21       seal       orca ## 4        deer polar_bear ## 19        rat polar_bear ## 2         cod polar_bear ## 8        orca polar_bear ## 6        lynx polar_bear ## 22       seal polar_bear ## 12    plant_1        rat ## 15    plant_2       seal

title: Building a Metaweb
text: metaweb represents set potential consumer–resource interactions system. context paleoecology, metaweb captures interactions trait-compatible, even may occur simultaneously realised community. PFWIM workflow allows users infer potential interactions species trait data categorical feeding rules. vignette demonstrates : * Infer metaweb edgelist using infer_edgelist() * Convert edgelist igraph network * Visualise resulting food web
code: library(pfwim) library(dplyr) library(igraph)  data("traits", package = "pfwim") data("feeding_rules", package = "pfwim")

title: Building a Metaweb
text: function infer_edgelist() evaluates trait compatibility species according set categorical feeding rules. returns edgelist, row represents feasible interaction. Typical edgelists contain: consumer – feeding species resource – prey species edges define structure potential food web.
code: metaweb_el <- infer_edgelist(   data = traits,   cat_combo_list = feeding_rules,   col_taxon = "species",   certainty_req = "all",   hide_printout = TRUE )  head(metaweb_el) ## # A tibble: 6 × 2 ##   taxon_resource taxon_consumer ##   <chr>          <chr>          ## 1 cod            orca           ## 2 cod            polar_bear     ## 3 deer           lynx           ## 4 deer           polar_bear     ## 5 lynx           lynx           ## 6 lynx           polar_bear

what: Converting the Edgelist to an igraph Network
title: Building a Metaweb
text: edgelist can directly converted igraph object, allows users compute network statistics generate visualisations.
code: metaweb_graph <- graph_from_data_frame(   metaweb_el,   directed = TRUE )  metaweb_graph ## IGRAPH 21a7c06 DN-- 10 22 --  ## + attr: name (v/c) ## + edges from 21a7c06 (vertex names): ##  [1] cod       ->orca       cod       ->polar_bear deer      ->lynx       ##  [4] deer      ->polar_bear lynx      ->lynx       lynx      ->polar_bear ##  [7] orca      ->orca       orca      ->polar_bear plankton  ->cod        ## [10] plankton  ->seal       plant_1   ->deer       plant_1   ->rat        ## [13] plant_1   ->seal       plant_2   ->deer       plant_2   ->seal       ## [16] polar_bear->orca       polar_bear->polar_bear rat       ->lynx       ## [19] rat       ->polar_bear seal      ->lynx       seal      ->orca       ## [22] seal      ->polar_bear

title: Building a Metaweb
text: Food webs directed networks edges flow resource → consumer.  visualisation represents potential trophic structure community based purely trait compatibility. feasible interactions included, metawebs typically much denser observed ecological networks.
code: set.seed(66)  plot(   metaweb_graph,   vertex.size = 35,   vertex.label.cex = 0.6,   edge.arrow.size = 0.3,   layout = layout_with_fr(metaweb_graph),   main = "Metaweb" )

title: Generating Realised Food Webs
text: metaweb contains trait-compatible interactions, real ecological networks typically contain far fewer links. simulate realistic food webs, PFWIM provides function powerlaw_prey(), downsamples interactions metaweb according power-law prey degree distribution. vignette demonstrates : Generate metaweb edgelist Downsample interactions create realised webs Compare metaweb realised networks using igraph
code: library(pfwim) library(dplyr) library(igraph)  data("traits", package = "pfwim") data("feeding_rules", package = "pfwim")

title: Generating Realised Food Webs
code: metaweb_el <- infer_edgelist(   data = traits,   cat_combo_list = feeding_rules,   col_taxon = "species",   certainty_req = "all",   hide_printout = TRUE )

title: Generating Realised Food Webs
text: function powerlaw_prey() randomly samples prey consumer according power-law distribution, producing networks closely resemble empirical food webs. realised webs generated via stochastic downsampling, often useful generate multiple network realisations. allows users explore variability network structure perform simulation-based analyses. argument n_samp controls many realised webs generated. result list edgelists, element represents one simulated realised food web. entry list can accessed individually.
code: realised_webs <- powerlaw_prey(   el = metaweb_el,   n_samp = 5,   y = 2.5 ) length(realised_webs) ## [1] 5 realised_webs[[1]] ##      resource   consumer ## 9    plankton        cod ## 14    plant_2       deer ## 11    plant_1       deer ## 20       seal       lynx ## 3        deer       lynx ## 16 polar_bear       orca ## 7        orca       orca ## 2         cod polar_bear ## 22       seal polar_bear ## 4        deer polar_bear ## 19        rat polar_bear ## 12    plant_1        rat ## 10   plankton       seal realised_webs[[2]] ##    resource   consumer ## 9  plankton        cod ## 11  plant_1       deer ## 5      lynx       lynx ## 20     seal       lynx ## 3      deer       lynx ## 21     seal       orca ## 1       cod       orca ## 2       cod polar_bear ## 12  plant_1        rat ## 10 plankton       seal

title: Generating Realised Food Webs
text: generating multiple realised food webs, can useful construct single representative network summarises interactions observed across simulations. can done counting frequently interaction occurs across simulated webs. First, combine realised edgelists one table. .id column identifies realised web interaction came . Next, count often interaction appears across simulations. column freq indicates number realised webs interaction occurs. simple consensus rule keep interactions appear least half simulations. produces consensus realised web.
code: library(dplyr)  combined_edges <- dplyr::bind_rows(   lapply(realised_webs, as.data.frame),   .id = "web_id" )  head(combined_edges) ##   web_id   resource consumer ## 1  web_1   plankton      cod ## 2  web_1    plant_2     deer ## 3  web_1    plant_1     deer ## 4  web_1       seal     lynx ## 5  web_1       deer     lynx ## 6  web_1 polar_bear     orca edge_frequency <- combined_edges %>%   count(resource, consumer, name = "freq")  edge_frequency ##      resource   consumer freq ## 1         cod       orca    2 ## 2         cod polar_bear    2 ## 3        deer       lynx    4 ## 4        deer polar_bear    2 ## 5        lynx       lynx    3 ## 6        lynx polar_bear    3 ## 7        orca       orca    3 ## 8        orca polar_bear    1 ## 9    plankton        cod    5 ## 10   plankton       seal    3 ## 11    plant_1       deer    3 ## 12    plant_1        rat    5 ## 13    plant_1       seal    3 ## 14    plant_2       deer    3 ## 15    plant_2       seal    2 ## 16 polar_bear       orca    2 ## 17 polar_bear polar_bear    1 ## 18        rat       lynx    3 ## 19        rat polar_bear    1 ## 20       seal       lynx    3 ## 21       seal       orca    2 ## 22       seal polar_bear    2 consensus_el <- edge_frequency %>%   filter(freq >= 3)

title: Generating Realised Food Webs
code: library(igraph)  consensus_graph <- graph_from_data_frame(   consensus_el,   directed = TRUE )  plot(   consensus_graph,   vertex.size = 35,   vertex.label.cex = 0.7,   edge.arrow.size = 0.3,   main = "Consensus Realised Web" )

title: Generating Realised Food Webs
text: Instead filtering interactions, one can construct weighted network edge weights represent interaction frequency. case, freq column becomes edge weight, representing consistently interaction occurs across simulations.
code: weighted_graph <- graph_from_data_frame(   edge_frequency,   directed = TRUE )  plot(   weighted_graph,   vertex.size = 35,   vertex.label.cex = 0.7,   edge.width = E(weighted_graph)$freq,   edge.arrow.size = 0.3,   main = "Weighted Realised Web" )

what: Infer trophic interactions using PFWIM trait rules — infer_edgelist
title: Infer trophic interactions using PFWIM trait rules — infer_edgelist
text: Infers consumer–resource edgelist using categorical trait matching rules based PFWIM (Paleo Food Web Inference Model) described Shaw (2024). Interactions inferred comparing resource consumer trait combinations set allowed trait rules.

title: Infer trophic interactions using PFWIM trait rules — infer_edgelist
code: infer_edgelist(   data,   cat_combo_list,   col_taxon = "taxon",   col_num_size = NULL,   cat_trait_types = NULL,   num_size_rule = NULL,   certainty_req = "all",   allow_self = TRUE,   return_full_matrix = FALSE,   print_dropped_taxa = FALSE,   hide_printout = FALSE,   ... )

title: Infer trophic interactions using PFWIM trait rules — infer_edgelist
text: data data.frame containing taxa associated trait values. row represents taxon column represents trait. cat_combo_list data.frame defining allowed consumer–resource trait combinations. Must contain columns: trait_type_resource Resource trait category trait_resource Resource trait value trait_type_consumer Consumer trait category trait_consumer Consumer trait value col_taxon Character string indicating column containing taxon names data. Default "taxon". col_num_size Optional column name containing numerical size values taxa. Used applying numeric predator–prey size rule. cat_trait_types Optional character vector specifying subset categorical trait columns use. NULL, traits appearing cat_combo_list used. num_size_rule Optional function defining predator–prey size feasibility rule. function must accept two numeric vectors: (resource_size, consumer_size) return 1 feasible interactions 0 otherwise. Example: function(res_size, con_size) { ifelse(res_size <= con_size, 1, 0) } certainty_req Defines many trait rules must satisfied interaction considered feasible. "" trait types must match numeric Minimum number matching trait types required allow_self Logical. TRUE, allows interactions resource consumer taxon (self-loops). Default FALSE. return_full_matrix Logical. TRUE, returns full matrix taxon pairs number matching trait rules. FALSE, returns inferred interactions edgelist. print_dropped_taxa Logical. TRUE, prints taxa removed inferred food web feasible interactions. hide_printout Logical. TRUE, suppresses progress messages. ... Additional arguments reserved future extensions.

title: Infer trophic interactions using PFWIM trait rules — infer_edgelist
text: return_full_matrix = FALSE: two-column matrix containing: taxon_resource Resource taxon taxon_consumer Consumer taxon return_full_matrix = TRUE: matrix containing taxon pairs number trait rules satisfied.

title: Infer trophic interactions using PFWIM trait rules — infer_edgelist
text: Trait matching performed across trait types present cat_combo_list. potential taxon pair, number satisfied trait rules calculated. interaction inferred number satisfied rules meets required threshold defined certainty_req. Optionally, numerical predator–prey size rule can also applied using num_size_rule. function evaluates possible consumer–resource taxon pairs determines interaction feasibility using categorical trait rules , optionally, numerical size constraint. final edgelist includes interactions meeting certainty requirement.

what: Generate hypothetical realised webs using a power-law link distribution — powerlaw_prey
title: Generate hypothetical realised webs using a power-law link distribution — powerlaw_prey
text: PFWIM generates series replicate hypothetical realised food webs reducing feasible links consumer match target link distribution. default distribution mixed exponential–power law -degree distribution described Shaw (2024) Roopnarine (2006).

title: Generate hypothetical realised webs using a power-law link distribution — powerlaw_prey
code: powerlaw_prey(   el,   n_samp = 50,   y = 2.5,   func = function(r, M, y) exp(-r/(exp((y - 1) * (log(M)/y)))) )

title: Generate hypothetical realised webs using a power-law link distribution — powerlaw_prey
text: el Data frame matrix containing feasible consumer–resource edgelist. Column 1 = resource, Column 2 = consumer. n_samp Integer. Number replicate realised webs generate. Default = 50. y Numeric. Parameter controlling shape power-law distribution. Default = 2.5. func Function. Probability function -degree r, total prey richness M, parameter y. Must return numeric value > 0. Default: function(r, M, y) exp(-r / (exp((y - 1) * (log(M) / y)))).

title: Generate hypothetical realised webs using a power-law link distribution — powerlaw_prey
text: list length n_samp. element data frame representing realised food web edgelist two columns: resource Resource species consumer Consumer species

title: Generate hypothetical realised webs using a power-law link distribution — powerlaw_prey
text: consumer el, number prey links realised web sampled according distribution defined func. sampled prey drawn randomly without exceeding maximum feasible prey consumer.

title: Generate hypothetical realised webs using a power-law link distribution — powerlaw_prey
text: Shaw, J. (2024). PFWIM: Paleo Food-web Inference Model. Preprint. Roopnarine, P. (2006). Palaeoecology food-web structure fossil communities.

title: Generate hypothetical realised webs using a power-law link distribution — powerlaw_prey
code: # Infer a minimal edgelist edgelist <- infer_edgelist(   data = data.frame(     species = c("plankton","plant_1","plant_2","cod","rat","deer"),     feeding = c("primary","primary","primary","secondary","secondary","secondary")   ),   cat_combo_list = data.frame(     trait_type_resource = c("feeding","feeding","feeding"),     trait_resource = c("primary","primary","primary"),     trait_type_consumer = c("feeding","feeding","feeding"),     trait_consumer = c("secondary","secondary","secondary")   ),   col_taxon = "species",   certainty_req = "all" ) #> [1] "feeding" #> [1] "0 taxa dropped from web"  # Generate realized webs webs <- powerlaw_prey(edgelist, n_samp = 3, y = 2.5)

title: Sample integers according to a discrete probability distribution — sample_pdf

code: sample_pdf(   M = 100,   y = 2.5,   func = function(r, M, y) exp(-r/(exp((y - 1) * (log(M)/y)))),   n_samp = 100 )

title: Sample integers according to a discrete probability distribution — sample_pdf
text: M Integer. Maximum value sample (upper bound 1:M). y Numeric. Parameter controlling distribution shape. func Function. Probability function r (1:M), M, y. Default PFWIM exponential–power law function: function(r, M, y) exp(-r / (exp((y - 1) * (log(M) / y)))). n_samp Integer. Number random draws.
